title: Sentinel perception benchmark — CPU vs AMD Instinct MI300X, FP32
record_note: Figures transcribed verbatim from a run of `python -m app.benchmark --compare cpu,rocm --parity` on the AMD host. Fields the report did not carry are null and labelled as not recorded; none has been inferred or filled in. `python -m app.benchmark ... --json` emits the harness's own complete record, which is the authoritative machine-readable form.

speedup.basis: same host, same workload, CPU baseline vs AMD ROCm

caveats: One clip, one host, one model, one resolution. This is a measurement of this workload on this machine, not a statement about general real-world performance.
FP32 only. No FP16, INT8, quantization, batching, ONNX Runtime, MIGraphX or TensorRT was used or measured.
Single-stream: frames are processed one at a time, as a live camera delivers them.
Model load time is measured and reported separately by the harness and is excluded from every throughput figure here.
The MI300X was a virtual function (VF) instance; a bare-metal card may behave differently.
